tools.name: get_entry
tools.title: Get an entry
tools.description: One entry, by VHID, short name or Wikidata QID: its public record (title, description, handles, image, URL) and, as `editing`, what the editor would load for this key — the current revision, the editable fields, every handle with who manages it (the Wikidata sync or the site), which fields the sync manages, and whether this key may edit it live. Without an API key, the public record alone.

entry.description: The entry: its VHID (11 digits), its short name (as in verifiedhandles.org/<short>), or its Wikidata QID (Q42).

include_platforms.description: Also list every platform a handle can be on (id, name, URL prefix). Needs an API key.

short.description: The entry’s short name (`/<short>`), if it has one.

entity_type.description: What it is, from its Wikidata item: `person`, `organization` or `brand`; null when unknown. `entity_kind` says more.

entity_kind.description: The finer kind of thing it is, from its Wikidata item’s classes; null when unknown (an organisation or a brand not yet read since kinds were added reads null until the sync next reads its item). Each kind belongs to one `entity_type`, and `person`, `organization` and `brand` are also the kinds of an entry of that type with no finer one. The kinds, with their type: `person` (person: person), `musical_group` (organization: musical group), `sports_organization` (organization: sports organisation), `broadcaster` (organization: broadcaster), `publisher` (organization: publisher), `educational_institution` (organization: educational institution), `research_organization` (organization: research organisation), `religious_organization` (organization: religious organisation), `museum` (organization: museum), `financial_institution` (organization: financial institution), `chain` (organization: retail or hospitality chain), `nonprofit` (organization: charity or non-profit), `company` (organization: company), `organization` (organization: organisation), `website` (brand: website or app), `brand` (brand: brand). New kinds may be added; treat an unknown value as its `entity_type`.

verified.description: Verified Handles has verified the entry.

description.description: The description as sanitised HTML, links to other entries named as they are today.

title.description: The page’s title, underscored (`Draft:` first for a draft).

adapted.description: Present and true when the text has been edited on the site since.

revision.description: The page’s revision the text was taken from: its permalink is `https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=<title>&oldid=<revision>`. Absent on a credit from before revisions were kept.

draft.description: Present and true when the page is an English Wikipedia draft (the Draft namespace), not yet an article.

anyOf.description: The English Wikipedia page an entry’s description was taken from: an article, or a draft (`draft: true`).

description_license.description: The description’s licence, as an SPDX id: `CC-BY-SA-4.0` when it was taken from Wikipedia (`description_source` is set), which means crediting the article and sharing alike. Null otherwise: the description is CC0 like the rest of the text.

image.description: The lead image (the same as `images[0].url`), or null.

license.description: An upload’s licence, by id. Null for a Commons image (see `license_name`) or when none was recorded.

license_name.description: The licence’s name, e.g. "CC BY-SA 4.0". Null until it is known.

freely_licensed.description: May be reused under a free licence. Null when no licence is recorded.

credit.description: The credit line to show when reusing the image.

source_page.description: The image’s Wikimedia Commons file page, which states its licence and author.

anyOf.description: Who owns an image and how it may be reused. An entry’s text is CC0 (bar a description taken from Wikipedia); its images are licensed separately, by their owners.

image_rights.description: The lead image’s rights, or null when there is no image.

url.description: The image, as a path on this site (`/img/w/480q75/<id>`).

main.description: True for the lead image, false for the gallery images after it.

license.description: An upload’s licence, by id. Null for a Commons image (see `license_name`) or when none was recorded.

license_name.description: The licence’s name, e.g. "CC BY-SA 4.0". Null until it is known.

freely_licensed.description: May be reused under a free licence. Null when no licence is recorded.

credit.description: The credit line to show when reusing the image.

source_page.description: The image’s Wikimedia Commons file page, which states its licence and author.

image_rights.description: Who owns an image and how it may be reused. An entry’s text is CC0 (bar a description taken from Wikipedia); its images are licensed separately, by their owners.

link.description: Where the image links on the entry page instead of opening the full-screen viewer, or null.

images.description: Every image the entry shows, the lead first. Empty when it shows none.

category.description: How the entry page groups it.

value.description: The handle as stored (a username, an id, a URL). Null for an email address, which is never published as data.

display.description: The label the entry page shows instead of the value, if an editor set one. Null for email.

url.description: The profile’s address, built from the platform’s URL pattern. Null for email.

verified.description: Verified Handles has checked that this account belongs to the entry.

checked.description: What Verified Handles’ own handle checker found when it last looked at this account, from the platform’s official API: only on YouTube (channel and handle), Deezer and GitHub, and only for a look at most 7 days old. Absent otherwise. The entry page shows it only for `dead` (“Not found when checked …”) and `renamed`.

verdict.description: `live`: the profile was there. `dead`: the platform did not find it. `renamed`: it answers under another name. `unknown`: the platform gave no answer a rule could read.

now.description: For `renamed`, the name it answers to now, when the platform gave one. A YouTube handle’s is lowercase.

items.description: One account or identifier of an entry, in the order the entry page shows them. A Wikidata item linked to the entry comes last, as platform `wikidata`.

anyOf.description: An entry: the same data its page shows, from the same code. Email addresses are masked. The text is CC0, except a description taken from Wikipedia (`description_license`).

entry.description: The entry’s public record, as GET /api/v1/entities/{vhid} answers it. Null for a VHID that is not public (a deleted entry): `editing` says more.

editing.description: With an API key: what the editor loads for this key (GET /api/editor/{vhid}): `baseRevisionId`, `capabilities` (whether it may edit live or propose), `editable`, `handles`, `provenance` (which fields the Wikidata sync manages), `qid`, and `platforms` with include_platforms. Where the key may not open the editor, the route’s `status` and `error`. Absent with no key.

outputSchema.description: One entry: its public record and, with an API key, what the editor would load for it.

tools.name: search_entries
tools.title: Search entries
tools.description: Search the entries as the site search does: words match titles, subtitles and descriptions; a Wikidata QID finds the entries linked to it; a VHID finds that entry and the entries that link to it.

query.description: The query as it was read: trimmed and cut to 100 characters.

total.description: How many entries matched in all.

limit.description: The page size used: the `limit` asked for, clamped to the endpoint’s range.

offset.description: The offset used: the `offset` asked for, clamped to 0–10,000.

next_offset.description: The `offset` of the next page, or null when this is the last one. Follow it rather than computing it.

short.description: The entry’s short name (`/<short>`), if it has one.

snippet.description: Plain text from the description around the words that matched, or null when the match was not in it.

highlighted.description: `snippet` is a real excerpt (true), or there is none (false).

tools.name: find_by_handle
tools.title: Find entries by handle
tools.description: Which public entries list a handle: “is x.com/someone an official account, and whose?”. Give a profile’s address as url (https://x.com/someone), or platform (its catalog id: twitter, instagram, youtube, …) and value (someone or @someone). Answers each entry’s VHID, title and URL, the handle as the entry lists it, and whether that handle is verified; an empty list when no entry lists it. Case is ignored where the platform ignores it. Email addresses are not looked up.

url.description: A profile’s address, such as https://x.com/someone. Instead of platform and value.

platform.description: The platform’s catalog id, such as twitter. With value.

value.description: The handle on that platform, such as someone or @someone.

platform.description: The platform looked on: the one asked, or the one whose address `url` is.

value.description: The handle looked up, as the site stores one: from `url`, what follows the platform’s address.
The handle as the entry lists it: on a platform that ignores case, its case may differ from the value asked.

verified.description: Whether the handle itself is verified on this entry (not the entry’s own badge).

items.description: An entry that lists the handle.

results.description: Verified handles first, then by VHID; at most 50. Empty when no public entry lists it.

outputSchema.description: The public entries that list a handle.

tools.name: get_entry_history
tools.title: Entry history
tools.description: An entry’s public edit history, newest first (`next_offset` pages on). A merged entry’s key gives its own history.

entry.description: The entry: its VHID (11 digits), its short name (as in verifiedhandles.org/<short>), or its Wikidata QID (Q42).

merged_into.description: Present when the entry was merged into another: that entry’s VHID. The history is still the merged entry’s own.

limit.description: The page size used: the `limit` asked for, clamped to the endpoint’s range.

offset.description: The offset used: the `offset` asked for, clamped to 0–10,000.

next_offset.description: The `offset` of the next page, or null when this is the last one. Follow it rather than computing it.

ref_id.description: The revision’s id: `a<n>` for the history kept from the old wiki, `r<n>` for an edit made since.

kind.description: `archive`: from the old wiki. `forward`: made on Verified Handles.

actor.description: Who made it, as they chose to be named in public; null when they keep their name private.

is_bot.description: Made by an automated process (the Wikidata sync, an import).

hidden.description: Always false here: a hidden revision is never in the public history.

deleted.description: Always false here: a deleted revision is never in the public history.

proposer.description: For an approved proposal, who proposed it, as they chose to be named; null otherwise.

items.description: One revision in an entry’s public history.

outputSchema.description: A page of an entry’s public revision history, newest first.

tools.name: get_entries
tools.title: Get many entries
tools.description: Up to 50 entries’ public records in one call, by VHID or short name (not a Wikidata QID: get_entry or search_entries finds an entry by its item), each answered as get_entry answers it signed out — the entry, or not_found — in the order given. A name given twice is answered once.

entries.description: The entries: each a VHID (11 digits) or a short name.

key.description: The key as asked for, trimmed.

short.description: The entry’s short name (`/<short>`), if it has one.
